## The question

What does a clean, reproducible regional map of Poland look like when built entirely in R,
from download to exported PNG?

## Data

- Boundaries: Eurostat GISCO NUTS-2 regions, via the `giscoR` package
- Projection: ETRS89 / Poland CS92 (EPSG:2180), the national standard

## The map


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(sf)
library(giscoR)
library(tmap)

pl <- gisco_get_nuts(country = "PL", nuts_level = 2,
                     year = "2021", resolution = "10") |>
  st_transform(2180)

pl$area_km2 <- as.numeric(st_area(pl)) / 1e6

tm_shape(pl) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "area_km2",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.yl_gn_bu"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Area (km²)")) +
  tm_text("NAME_LATN", size = 0.5) +
  tm_title("Poland: NUTS-2 regions") +
  tm_credits("Data: © EuroGeographics / GISCO · Map: Truc Pham", position = c("left", "bottom"))
```

## What I learned

- Always reproject before measuring area: in geographic degrees the numbers are meaningless.
- `tmap` v4 uses `fill =` and `tm_scale_*()`, not the older `col =` / `palette =` arguments.

## Next time

Swap area for a real indicator (e.g. population density from GUS) and try a
`ggplot2` + `geom_sf()` version for comparison.
